question: Did the forest that was lost between 1984 and 2022 come back, and where?
answer: Across the mapped extent 101,754,164 ha of forest was lost at least once. 39,562,228 ha held forest again for three consecutive years and is counted as recovered; the remaining 62,191,936 ha is not. This measures return of tree cover, not return of the forest that was there: species, age and structure are outside what a cover mask can see, and no gain product was used, so forest appearing where nothing was lost is not counted at all.

partition.note: Every lost cell is in exactly one of the two buckets. Nothing else may be added to them.

unconfirmedReturns.emittedRuleText: a return with fewer than the required consecutive years by 2022 is reported separately and counted as neither recovered nor not-recovered
unconfirmedReturns.whatTheNumbersShow: Unconfirmed returns are not a third bucket. They overlap the other two: a cell mid-return in 2022 is counted as not recovered, and a cell that recovered from an earlier loss and is mid-return from a later one is counted as both recovered and unconfirmed. The worker's own hand-worked test pins that overlap deliberately.
unconfirmedReturns.finding: The run emitted rule text saying an unconfirmed return is 'counted as neither recovered nor not-recovered'. Its arithmetic does the opposite, and the arithmetic is the tested behaviour. Anyone who read the emitted text would subtract these cells from the not-recovered total and understate it by the figure above. The run output is left as it was written; the worker's text is corrected so no later run repeats the claim.
unconfirmedReturns.severity: misstatement in emitted prose, not in any counted number

boundaryCoverage.whyDistrictsAreMissing: The worker drops a district that holds no cell it can count, so 183 of the 343 districts in the 2023 representation order do not appear in its output at all. A reader cannot tell that apart from a district lost to a bug, which is why it is written down here rather than inferred.
boundaryCoverage.corroboration: The interval zonal worker is a separate program that read the same boundary edition against the same mapped extent. It reports all 343 districts and puts exactly zero mapped cells in each of the 183, and its mapped-cell total agrees with the recovery run's district total to the cell. Two independently written workers reaching the same partition is what makes the omission a reporting gap rather than a measurement one.
boundaryCoverage.whyAreaFallsOutsideEveryDistrict: The mapped extent is a raster and the districts are polygons that stop at the coast. Cells the product mapped over water and over the seaward edge of the shoreline belong to no district. The interval zonal worker sees the same residual, so it is a property of the two geometries and not of this run.

notMeasured: Forest appearing where none was lost. That needs a validated gain product and this pipeline has none.
Whether what returned is the same forest. A cover mask sees canopy, not species, age or structure.
Anything outside the land-cover product's mapped extent, which stays Unknown and is never read as zero.
